requirements.requirement: The system must compute an appropriateness score per provider based on alignment between prescribed drugs and mapped conditions.
The system must normalize appropriateness scores to a consistent scale (0–100).
The system must weight prescription volume when calculating appropriateness scores.
The system must compare prescribed drugs against expected condition-treatment mappings derived from ICD-10 associations.
The system must flag prescriptions that do not match any known condition-treatment mapping.
The system must invoke an LLM to infer condition-treatment relationships when deterministic mappings are missing.
The system must ensure LLM outputs are structured into a standardized mapping format before use in scoring.
The system must incorporate LLM-inferred mappings into the scoring calculation only when confidence exceeds a defined threshold.
The system must log LLM-derived mappings and associated confidence scores for auditability.
The system must produce consistent scores for identical input datasets across repeated runs.
The system must handle cases where a provider has no prescribing data by returning a null or explicitly defined default score.
The system must handle cases where condition mappings are incomplete by still producing a partial score using available data.
The system must ensure that ambiguous drug-condition relationships are resolved via LLM synthesis rather than discarded.
The system must cap the influence of any single drug or condition on the final appropriateness score.
